text: If every wheel on Earth vanished tonight, you wouldn't make it to work tomorrow. And that's the least of your problems.
Every car, bus and train would drop onto its axles, turning every highway into one giant parking lot.
But gears are just wheels with teeth. So your watch, your engine, and every power plant stop too.
Turbines stop spinning, the power grid collapses, and the whole planet goes dark.
Without trucks, supermarket shelves would be empty in about three days.
Planes are grounded too. No landing gear, and no spinning turbines in the jet engines.
So we'd move heavy things the ancient way: dragging them on sledges.
But here's the crazy part. The wheel was only invented about five and a half thousand years ago... and not for carts.
It was for making pottery. So if wheels vanished, someone would probably reinvent them within a week.
Because the wheel isn't just an invention. It's what holds the modern world together.
